text: Model Selection via Information Criteria
code: # Generate data from EKw distribution set.seed(456) n <- 1500 data_ekw <- rekw(n, alpha = 2, beta = 3, lambda = 1.5)  # Define candidate models models <- list(   Beta = list(     fn = llbeta,     gr = grbeta,     start = c(2, 2),     npar = 2   ),   Kw = list(     fn = llkw,     gr = grkw,     start = c(2, 3),     npar = 2   ),   EKw = list(     fn = llekw,     gr = grekw,     start = c(2, 3, 1.5),     npar = 3   ),   Mc = list(     fn = llmc,     gr = grmc,     start = c(2, 2, 1.5),     npar = 3   ) )  # Fit all models results_list <- lapply(names(models), function(name) {   m <- models[[name]]   fit <- optim(     par = m$start,     fn = m$fn,     gr = m$gr,     data = data_ekw,     method = "BFGS"   )    loglik <- -fit$value   data.frame(     Model = name,     nPar = m$npar,     LogLik = loglik,     AIC = -2 * loglik + 2 * m$npar,     BIC = -2 * loglik + m$npar * log(n),     Converged = fit$convergence == 0   ) })  # Combine results comparison <- do.call(rbind, results_list) comparison <- comparison[order(comparison$AIC), ] rownames(comparison) <- NULL  knitr::kable(comparison,   digits = 2,   caption = "Model Selection via Information Criteria" )

title: Introduction to gkwdist: Generalized Kumaraswamy Distribution Family
text: Profile likelihood provides accurate confidence intervals Wald intervals, especially small samples near parameter boundaries.
code: # Generate data set.seed(789) data_profile <- rkw(500, alpha = 2.5, beta = 3.5)  # Fit model fit_profile <- optim(   par = c(2, 3),   fn = llkw,   gr = grkw,   data = data_profile,   method = "BFGS",   hessian = TRUE )  mle_profile <- fit_profile$par  # Compute profile likelihood for alpha alpha_grid <- seq(mle_profile[1] - 1, mle_profile[1] + 1, length.out = 50) alpha_grid <- alpha_grid[alpha_grid > 0] profile_ll <- numeric(length(alpha_grid))  for (i in seq_along(alpha_grid)) {   profile_fit <- optimize(     f = function(beta) llkw(c(alpha_grid[i], beta), data_profile),     interval = c(0.1, 10),     maximum = FALSE   )   profile_ll[i] <- -profile_fit$objective }  # Plot  # Profile likelihood chi_crit <- qchisq(0.95, df = 1) threshold <- max(profile_ll) - chi_crit / 2  plot(alpha_grid, profile_ll,   type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#2E4057",   main = "Profile Log-Likelihood",   xlab = expression(alpha), ylab = "Profile Log-Likelihood", las = 1 ) abline(v = mle_profile[1], col = "#8B0000", lty = 2, lwd = 2) abline(v = 2.5, col = "#006400", lty = 2, lwd = 2) abline(h = threshold, col = "#808080", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5) legend("topright",   legend = c("MLE", "True", "95% CI"),   col = c("#8B0000", "#006400", "#808080"),   lty = c(2, 2, 3), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8 ) grid(col = "gray90") # Wald vs Profile CI comparison se_profile <- sqrt(diag(solve(fit_profile$hessian))) wald_ci <- mle_profile[1] + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_profile[1] profile_ci <- range(alpha_grid[profile_ll >= threshold])  plot(1:2, c(mle_profile[1], mle_profile[1]),   xlim = c(0.5, 2.5),   ylim = range(c(wald_ci, profile_ci)),   pch = 19, col = "#8B0000", cex = 1.5,   main = "Confidence Interval Comparison",   xlab = "", ylab = expression(alpha), xaxt = "n", las = 1 ) axis(1, at = 1:2, labels = c("Wald", "Profile"))  # Add CIs segments(1, wald_ci[1], 1, wald_ci[2], lwd = 3, col = "#2E4057") segments(2, profile_ci[1], 2, profile_ci[2], lwd = 3, col = "#8B0000") abline(h = 2.5, col = "#006400", lty = 2, lwd = 2)  legend("topright",   legend = c("MLE", "True", "Wald 95% CI", "Profile 95% CI"),   col = c("#8B0000", "#006400", "#2E4057", "#8B0000"),   pch = c(19, NA, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 2, 1, 1),   lwd = c(NA, 2, 3, 3), bty = "n", cex = 0.8 ) grid(col = "gray90")

title: Introduction to gkwdist: Generalized Kumaraswamy Distribution Family
text: multivariate inference, confidence ellipses show joint uncertainty parameter estimates.
code: # Compute variance-covariance matrix vcov_matrix <- solve(fit_profile$hessian)  # Create confidence ellipse (95%) theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) chi2_val <- qchisq(0.95, df = 2)  eig_decomp <- eigen(vcov_matrix) ellipse <- matrix(NA, nrow = 100, ncol = 2)  for (i in 1:100) {   v <- c(cos(theta[i]), sin(theta[i]))   ellipse[i, ] <- mle_profile + sqrt(chi2_val) *     (eig_decomp$vectors %*% diag(sqrt(eig_decomp$values)) %*% v) }  # Marginal CIs se_marg <- sqrt(diag(vcov_matrix)) ci_alpha_marg <- mle_profile[1] + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_marg[1] ci_beta_marg <- mle_profile[2] + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_marg[2]  # Plot plot(ellipse[, 1], ellipse[, 2],   type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#2E4057",   main = "95% Joint Confidence Region",   xlab = expression(alpha), ylab = expression(beta), las = 1 )  # Add marginal CIs abline(v = ci_alpha_marg, col = "#808080", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5) abline(h = ci_beta_marg, col = "#808080", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5)  # Add points points(mle_profile[1], mle_profile[2], pch = 19, col = "#8B0000", cex = 1.5) points(2.5, 3.5, pch = 17, col = "#006400", cex = 1.5)  legend("topright",   legend = c("MLE", "True", "Joint 95% CR", "Marginal 95% CI"),   col = c("#8B0000", "#006400", "#2E4057", "#808080"),   pch = c(19, 17, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, NA, 1, 3),   lwd = c(NA, NA, 2, 1.5), bty = "n" ) grid(col = "gray90")

title: On the Statistical Properties and Computational Inference of the Generalized Kumaraswamy Distribution Family
text: analysis continuous random variables constrained unit interval (0,1)(0,1) arises naturally numerous statistical applications, including proportions, rates, percentages, index measurements. classical Beta distribution (Johnson et al., 1995) long served canonical model data, offering analytical tractability well-understood properties. However, cumulative distribution function (CDF) involves incomplete beta function, requiring numerical evaluation special functions quantile computation simulation. Kumaraswamy (1980) introduced alternative two-parameter family closed-form CDF quantile function, facilitating computational efficiency maintaining comparable flexibility Beta distribution. Jones (2009) demonstrated Kumaraswamy distribution exhibits similar shape characteristics Beta family offering superior computational advantages. Building upon foundations, Carrasco, Ferrari Cordeiro (2010) introduced five-parameter Generalized Kumaraswamy (GKw) distribution combining Kumaraswamy CDF generalized-beta generator. Cordeiro de Castro (2011) developed related Kumaraswamy-generated (Kw-G) family, conceptually connected five-parameter GKw model studied . GKw distribution encompasses rich hierarchy submodels provides substantial flexibility modeling diverse patterns bounded data. Identifiability issues class revisited explicitly Carrasco Cordeiro (2017), likelihood asymptotics must stated conditionally regular identifiable parameter region. Despite theoretical appeal, fully explicit internally consistent analytical treatment GKw family—particularly likelihood-based inference—remained incomplete literature. vignette fills gap providing rigorous development, including validated expressions first second derivatives log-likelihood function, written form convenient implementation gkwdist R package.

title: gkwdist: Generalized Kumaraswamy Distribution Family
text: gkwdist implements Generalized Kumaraswamy (GKw) distribution seven nested sub-models bounded continuous data (0,1)(0,1) — proportions, rates, shares, indices. provides density, distribution, quantile random generation functions, analytical log-likelihood, score Hessian functions, written C++ via RcppArmadillo. Seven nested distributions one naming rule: prefix + family code. ll*, gr* hs* drop straight stats::optim — one pass data, substantially faster numerical (Richardson) differentiation. Numerically stable log space observations near boundaries, densities carry limiting value x=0x = 0 x=1x = 1 base R .

text: Maximum likelihood, analytical gradient observed information: gkwgetstartvalues() returns named vector already order family’s ll* expects — differs families, worth checking cheat sheet writing par hand.
code: library(gkwdist)  x <- seq(0.01, 0.99, length.out = 100)  dgkw(x, alpha = 2, beta = 3, gamma = 1.5, delta = 2, lambda = 1.2)  # density pgkw(x, 2, 3, 1.5, 2, 1.2)                                          # CDF qgkw(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), 2, 3, 1.5, 2, 1.2)                         # quantiles  set.seed(123) sample <- rgkw(1000, 2, 3, 1.5, 2, 1.2)                             # simulate set.seed(2024) data <- rkw(2000, alpha = 2.5, beta = 3.5)  fit <- optim(   par     = gkwgetstartvalues(data, family = "kw"),   fn      = llkw,   # negative log-likelihood   gr      = grkw,   # negative score   data    = data,   method  = "BFGS",   hessian = TRUE )  est <- fit$par se  <- sqrt(diag(solve(fit$hessian))) cbind(Estimate = est, Lower = est - 1.96 * se, Upper = est + 1.96 * se)

text: probability density function (PDF) calculated function corresponds standard Beta distribution \(Beta(\gamma, \delta+1)\): $$ f(x; \gamma, \delta) = \frac{x^{\gamma-1} (1-x)^{(\delta+1)-1}}{B(\gamma, \delta+1)} = \frac{x^{\gamma-1} (1-x)^{\delta}}{B(\gamma, \delta+1)} $$ \(0 < x < 1\), \(B(,b)\) Beta function (beta). specific parameterization arises special case five-parameter Generalized Kumaraswamy (GKw) distribution (dgkw) obtained setting parameters \(\alpha = 1\), \(\beta = 1\), \(\lambda = 1\). therefore equivalent McDonald (Mc)/Beta Power distribution (dmc) \(\lambda = 1\). text: Exponentiated Kumaraswamy (EKw) distribution GKw distribution (dekw) \(\gamma=1\) \(\delta=0\). probability density function (PDF) : $$ f(x | \theta) = \lambda \alpha \beta x^{\alpha-1} (1 - x^\alpha)^{\beta-1} \bigl[1 - (1 - x^\alpha)^\beta \bigr]^{\lambda - 1} $$ \(0 < x < 1\) \(\theta = (\alpha, \beta, \lambda)\). log-likelihood function \(\ell(\theta | \mathbf{x})\) sample \(\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_n)\) \(\sum_{=1}^n \ln f(x_i | \theta)\): $$ \ell(\theta | \mathbf{x}) = n[\ln(\lambda) + \ln(\alpha) + \ln(\beta)] + \sum_{=1}^{n} [(\alpha-1)\ln(x_i) + (\beta-1)\ln(v_i) + (\lambda-1)\ln(w_i)] $$ : \(v_i = 1 - x_i^{\alpha}\) \(w_i = 1 - v_i^{\beta} = 1 - (1-x_i^{\alpha})^{\beta}\) function computes returns negative log-likelihood, \(-\ell(\theta|\mathbf{x})\), suitable minimization using optimization routines like optim. Numerical stability maintained similarly llgkw.

title: Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of the EKw Distribution — pekw
text: Exponentiated Kumaraswamy (EKw) distribution special case five-parameter Generalized Kumaraswamy distribution (pgkw) obtained setting parameters \(\gamma = 1\) \(\delta = 0\). CDF GKw distribution \(F_{GKw}(q) = I_{y(q)}(\gamma, \delta+1)\), \(y(q) = [1-(1-q^{\alpha})^{\beta}]^{\lambda}\) \(I_x(,b)\) regularized incomplete beta function (pbeta). Setting \(\gamma=1\) \(\delta=0\) gives \(I_{y(q)}(1, 1)\). Since \(I_x(1, 1) = x\), CDF simplifies \(y(q)\): $$ F(q; \alpha, \beta, \lambda) = \bigl[1 - (1 - q^\alpha)^\beta \bigr]^\lambda $$ \(0 < q < 1\). implementation uses closed-form expression efficiency handles lower.tail log.p arguments appropriately.

title: Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of the Generalized Kumaraswamy Distribution — pgkw
text: cumulative distribution function (CDF) Generalized Kumaraswamy (GKw) distribution parameters alpha (\(\alpha\)), beta (\(\beta\)), gamma (\(\gamma\)), delta (\(\delta\)), lambda (\(\lambda\)) given : $$ F(q; \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta, \lambda) =   I_{x(q)}(\gamma, \delta+1) $$ \(x(q) = [1-(1-q^{\alpha})^{\beta}]^{\lambda}\) \(I_x(, b)\) regularized incomplete beta function, defined : $$ I_x(, b) = \frac{B_x(, b)}{B(, b)} = \frac{\int_0^x t^{-1}(1-t)^{b-1} dt}{\int_0^1 t^{-1}(1-t)^{b-1} dt} $$ corresponds pbeta function R, \(F(q; \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta, \lambda) = \code{pbeta}(x(q), \code{shape1} = \gamma, \code{shape2} = \delta+1)\). GKw distribution includes several special cases, Kumaraswamy, Beta, Exponentiated Kumaraswamy distributions (see dgkw details). function utilizes numerical algorithms computing regularized incomplete beta function accurately, especially near boundaries.

title: Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of the KKw Distribution — pkkw
text: Kumaraswamy-Kumaraswamy (KKw) distribution special case five-parameter Generalized Kumaraswamy distribution (pgkw) obtained setting shape parameter \(\gamma = 1\). title: gkwdist 1.1.3
text: llgkw() invalid parameter return (gkw.cpp): Fixed critical error negative log-likelihood returned R_NegInf (−∞) invalid parameters instead R_PosInf (+∞). Gradient-based MLE optimizers interpret −∞ global minimum, causing converge invalid boundary rather true MLE. gkwinit.cpp — delta validation (gkwinit.cpp): Fixed internal gkw_pdf() rejecting delta = 0 (valid GKw parameter value) due strict delta <= 0 check delta < 0. gkwinit.cpp — EKw/Kw sub-family PDF mapping (gkwinit.cpp): Fixed ekw_pdf() kw_pdf() passing delta = 1 instead correct delta = 0 delegating gkw_pdf(). EKw Kw GKw sub-families delta = 0, delta = 1. produced wrong starting values MLE families. hsbkw() — v^(β−1) computation (bkw.cpp): Fixed Hessian BKw negative log-likelihood returning wrong value β < 1. ternary expression (beta > 1.0) ? v_beta/v : 1.0 coincidentally produces correct result β = 1 wrong 0 < β < 1. Replaced exact formula safe_exp((beta - 1.0) * ln_v).

title: gkwdist 1.1.3
text: safe_exp() underflow scaling (utils.h): Fixed systematic 10× error moderate-underflow branch. previous implementation used DBL_MIN_SAFE * exp(x − log(DBL_MIN)) DBL_MIN_SAFE = 10 * DBL_MIN, yielding 10 * exp(x) instead exp(x). fix uses DBL_MIN * exp(x − log(DBL_MIN)) = exp(x) exactly. dgkw() silent boundary truncation removed (gkw.cpp): Removed block silently skipped data points within SQRT_EPSILON^(1/α) 0 1, returning density 0 points without warning. log-space computation handles near-boundary values correctly without truncation. llekw() / grekw() — lambda clamping removed (ekw.cpp): Removed arbitrary cap lambda_factor = min(lambda_factor, 1000) applied gradient Hessian terms λ > 1000. distorted optimization large-λ scenarios produced incorrect standard errors.

title: gkwdist 1.1.3
text: gkwinit.cpp: Removed using namespace Rcpp; file scope; replaced explicit Rcpp:: qualifications. Added NA/NaN filtering moment computation prevent silent corruption input data contains missing values. bkw.cpp: Removed spurious try/catch blocks wrapping Rcpp::<arma::vec>() conversions grbkw() hsbkw(). conversions throw context silent fallback masked type errors. gkw.cpp / ekw.cpp: Refactored Hessian accumulation build upper triangle inside observation loop symmetrize afterwards arma::symmatu(), eliminating O(n × p²) redundant assignments. utils.h — vec_safe_pow() UB guard: Added guard preventing undefined behaviour casting large y_rounded values (> INT_MAX) int odd-exponent sign detection. utils.h — vec_safe_pow() SIMD fast path: Added early-return path arma::exp(y * arma::log(x)) common case (y > 0, x > 0) fully auto-vectorizable, improving throughput gradient/Hessian evaluation.

title: gkwdist 1.1.1
text: Unified utility functions: Introduced utils.h header providing numerically stable implementations critical functions: log1mexp(): Stable computation log(1 - exp(x)) using Mächler (2012) methodology log1pexp(): Overflow-protected computation log(1 + exp(x)) safe_log(), safe_exp(), safe_pow(): Protected arithmetic operations graceful handling edge cases Vectorized versions (vec_safe_log, vec_log1mexp, etc.) efficient array operations Consistent parameter validation: distribution families now use dedicated parameter checkers (check_pars(), check_kw_pars(), check_ekw_pars(), etc.) properly handle NaN, Inf, boundary conditions. Complete documentation: C++ source files now include comprehensive Doxygen-style documentation headers describing: Mathematical formulas PDF, CDF, quantile, random generation Parameter constraints special cases Numerical stability considerations Relationship parent GKw distribution

title: gkwdist 1.1.1
text: Fixed critical bug qgkw(): Corrected logic error lower_tail transformation incorrectly applied log_p = TRUE. probability now properly converted linear scale tail adjustment. Fixed gradient calculation grkkw(): Resolved issue log_z recomputed clamping z minimum threshold, causing corrupted gradient values near boundaries. Fixed Hessian calculation hsmc(): Corrected sign errors formula lambda component Hessian matrix Beta-Power/McDonald distribution. Fixed gradient signs grmc(): Ensured consistent computation log-likelihood gradient negation optimization.

title: gkwdist 1.1.1
text: Eliminated unused variables: Removed declared unused constants (exp_threshold) intermediate variables across distribution files. Removed redundant calculations: Streamlined computations, notably pgkw() logarithm computed twice quantity. Simplified parameter recycling: Replaced double-modulo indexing pattern (idx = % k; vec[idx % vec.n_elem]) direct single-modulo access (vec[% vec.n_elem]) random generation functions. Standardized function signatures: distribution functions now follow consistent patterns parameter order, validation, return value handling.
